origin.description: The most common collector becomes the default. Ties use the alphabetically first kind.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: The data, path, or collector this function accepts.

origin.details: The most common collector becomes the default. Ties use the alphabetically first kind.
origin.value: The same value readr 2.2.0 returns for this case, written as one line in the output.
origin.example:
condensed <- cols_condense(spec(read_csv(I("a,b,c\n1,2,x\n3,4,y"))))
paste(paste(names(condensed$cols), collapse = ","), class(condensed$default)[1], class(condensed$cols[[1]])[1], sep = ";")

translation.description: The most common collector becomes the default. Ties use the alphabetically first kind.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: The data, path, or collector this function accepts.

translation.details: The most common collector becomes the default. Ties use the alphabetically first kind.
translation.value: The same value readr 2.2.0 returns for this case, written as one line in the output.
translation.example:
condensed = cols_condense(spec(read_csv(I("a,b,c\n1,2,x\n3,4,y"), show_col_types=False)))
return ",".join(collector.fields.get("name", "") for collector in condensed.cols) + ";collector_" + condensed.default.kind + ";collector_" + condensed.cols[0].kind
